title: Corrective IR for Live Venues
description: A live six-channel hybrid system combining per-channel corrective FIRs for the initial response with a separately applied target-hall reverberation tail.
question: Can corrective IR make one venue sound like another?
body: Playing a target hall’s impulse response (IR) in another venue also adds the current venue’s response. I wanted to correct the current room’s coloration before adding the target hall’s reverberation.

I measured six surround-loudspeaker-to-microphone paths and used Python to align them with the target IR. I created a corrective FIR filter for each channel, focusing on the first 40 ms and the 125 Hz–4 kHz band. The filters use regularization to limit excessive gain.

Max/MSP applies a separate corrective filter to each of the six surround speakers in real time. Convology XT adds the target hall’s reverberation from about 200 ms onward. The main PA carries the direct sound.

At the fourth-row center, mean spectral error fell from 2.69 to 2.24 dB across six channels. This comparison uses the same path measurements that were used to create the filters. It does not establish improvement at other seats or a perceptual match to the target hall.

plannedSubmission.venue: SA4ME: International Workshop on Spatial Audio for Multisensory Experiences · IEEE VR 2027

description.en: I plan to submit a paper on this Corrective IR project to SA4ME at IEEE VR 2027. The paper has not yet been submitted or accepted. If accepted, it is expected to be published in the IEEE Xplore Digital Library.
description.ko: 이 보정 IR 프로젝트를 IEEE VR 2027의 SA4ME 워크숍에 논문으로 제출할 예정입니다. 아직 제출·채택 전이며, 채택될 경우 IEEE Xplore Digital Library에 출판될 예정입니다.

summary.en: Built a six-channel correction system. At one position, mean spectral error fell from 2.69 to 2.24 dB.
summary.ko: 6채널 보정 시스템을 만들었고, 한 측정 위치에서 평균 스펙트럼 오차가 2.69→2.24 dB로 줄었습니다.

problem.en: I asked how to reduce the current venue’s effect when playing a target hall IR through its speakers.
problem.ko: 공연장에서 다른 공연장의 IR을 컨볼루션할 때 현재 공연장의 IR이 다시 더해지는 문제를 다뤘습니다.

design.en: I captured six surround-speaker responses and built a live system that corrects the early response and adds the target reverberation separately.
design.ko: 여섯 개의 서라운드 스피커 경로를 캡처하고 초기 응답 보정과 목표 잔향을 따로 처리하는 실시간 시스템을 만들었습니다.

analysis.en: I compared the first 40 ms in the 125 Hz–4 kHz band at fourth-row center. Mean error fell from 2.69 to 2.24 dB using the data used to create the filters.
analysis.ko: 객석 4열 중앙에서 초기 40 ms·125 Hz–4 kHz 구간을 비교했습니다. 결과적으로 필터 생성에 사용한 자료에서 평균 오차가 2.69→2.24 dB로 줄었습니다.

tools.en: I used Python for IR alignment and filter generation, and Max/MSP and Convology XT for playback. AI helped me write the Python code.
tools.ko: Python으로 IR 정렬과 필터 생성을, Max/MSP와 Convology XT로 실시간 처리를 했습니다. Python 코드 작성에는 AI의 도움을 받았습니다.

title: Sound xR Image Renderer Study
description: A black-box measurement study of how Sound xR Image maps loudspeaker geometry, Object position, and renderer parameters to output gains.
question: How does Sound xR turn position into speaker levels?
body: After using Sound xR Image for an outdoor performance, I wanted to understand how its settings affect the output level of each speaker. I changed speaker coordinates and IDs, Object position, XY mode, Size, Precision, and Distance Attenuation, and recorded the electrical output gains.

I compared the recorded gains with possible mathematical models. In the tested normal-output regions, inverse-distance weighting and power normalization matched representative data within about 0.005 dB. This describes observed behavior; it does not identify Yamaha’s internal implementation.

A fixed-segment model failed to predict the new five-speaker N/T tests. A different segment fitted N after I saw the measurements, but did not provide a general rule for T. That failure changed how I interpreted boundary behavior.
The next step is to fix a prediction rule before testing new layouts, and to investigate mode-dependent height control, Distance Attenuation, and moving sound sources.

summary.en: Tested how settings affect speaker gains. The distance model fits some conditions; boundary predictions failed.
summary.ko: 설정에 따른 스피커 출력 변화를 분석했습니다. 거리 모델은 일부 조건에 맞았지만 경계 구간의 예측은 실패했습니다.

problem.en: I investigated why speaker ID assignment and some boundary settings changed the output in ways a simple distance model could not explain.
problem.ko: 스피커 ID와 경계 구간의 출력이 단순 거리 모델의 예상과 달라지는 이유를 살펴봤습니다.

design.en: I changed coordinates, IDs, Object position, and renderer settings on a DME7 system, then recorded speaker output levels with Smaart.
design.ko: DME7에서 좌표·ID·Object 위치와 렌더러 설정을 바꾸고 Smaart로 스피커별 출력 레벨을 기록했습니다.

analysis.en: I compared the measurements with model predictions and revised my explanation after the five-speaker test failed.
analysis.ko: 측정값을 모델 예측과 비교했고, 5스피커 실험에서 예측이 실패한 뒤 해석을 수정했습니다.

tools.en: The report’s “supplied materials” are experiment.xlsx (366 rows), the AFC validation and revised technical review DOCX files, and testing result.rtf and final result.rtf. I used these records to write the analysis and report; the records do not specify the extent of AI assistance.
tools.ko: 보고서의 “supplied materials”는 experiment.xlsx(366행), AFC 검증·수정 기술 검토 DOCX 두 파일, testing result.rtf와 final result.rtf입니다. 이 기록을 바탕으로 분석과 보고서를 작성했으며, AI 지원 범위는 기록에서 확인되지 않습니다.

title: Multichannel Live Mixing
description: Exploring immersive sound image control and spatial mixing approaches for small performance venues.
question: Can sound placement match what audiences see?
body: I tested whether speaker placement and console routing could align the perceived direction of sound with what the audience sees on stage.
I built a 3.1 system with additional rear-stage speakers. Vocals, kick, snare, and bass went to the center; other instruments and reverberation were spread across the left, right, and rear speakers.

The sources were clearly separated, but informal audience feedback suggested they sounded disconnected. This led me to consider how listeners combine sounds into one scene. A structured listening test is still needed.

summary.en: Built a 3.1 system with rear speakers. Informal feedback suggested the sound felt too separated.
summary.ko: 3.1채널과 후방 스피커를 구성했습니다. 관객 반응에서 소리가 서로 떨어져 들리는 한계를 발견했습니다.

title: Real-Time Remote Multichannel Audio
description: Exploring real-time networked audio systems for remote musical interaction and collaboration.
question: Can musicians collaborate across distance?
body: I tested real-time multichannel audio transmission between two remote DAWs for recording, mixing, and performance.

I explored commercial network-audio approaches and tested relay and peer-to-peer tools, including ffmpeg, JACK Audio, and JackTrip. Audio could be sent, but playback did not remain sample-accurate over time.

The tests pointed to clock drift between the two systems as a key limitation. Over time, this was associated with buffer errors and audible clicks. Synchronization and adaptive resampling are next steps to investigate.

summary.en: Tested audio between remote DAWs. Clock drift limited stable playback over time.
summary.ko: 떨어진 DAW 사이의 오디오 전송을 시험했습니다. 시간이 지나며 쌓이는 클락 차이가 안정적인 재생을 제한했습니다.

title: Performer-Tailored Electronic Drum Module
description: A Max/MSP drum module with velocity zones and sample layers shaped around an individual performer’s dynamic range.
question: Can electronic drums adapt to each player’s touch?
body: The fixed response of a commercial electronic drum module may not match how a particular drummer plays. I built a Max/MSP module to adjust sample choice and playback level to one player’s striking range.

The patch routes MIDI notes to drum sounds and uses custom velocity ranges for snare and ride samples. MIDI velocity sets playback level, CC4 controls hi-hat openness, and the player can set gain, pan, and output for each drum.
The mapping is adjusted manually for one player. It does not learn automatically. Recorded velocity distributions and a controlled comparison with a fixed mapping are still needed.

summary.en: Built a Max/MSP drum module with manually adjusted velocity ranges for one player.
summary.ko: 한 연주자의 타격 범위에 맞춰 소리 반응을 수동으로 조절하는 Max/MSP 드럼 모듈을 만들었습니다.

problem.en: I wanted the electronic drum module’s response to match one player’s dynamics more closely.
problem.ko: 전자드럼의 소리 반응을 한 연주자의 연주 다이나믹에 맞추고 싶었습니다.

design.en: I built a Max/MSP module with adjustable snare and ride sample ranges, hi-hat control, and separate mixing settings for each drum.
design.ko: 스네어·라이드 샘플 선택 구간과 하이햇 반응, 드럼별 믹싱을 조절하는 Max/MSP 모듈을 만들었습니다.

analysis.en: I adjusted the mapping manually for one player. Velocity distributions and a before/after comparison are still needed.
analysis.ko: 한 연주자에 맞춰 소리 반응을 수동으로 조절했습니다. 타격 세기 분포와 조절 전후 비교는 추후 확인해야 합니다.

tools.en: I used Max/MSP and recorded drum audio samples. I used AI to gather information about Max/MSP objects.
tools.ko: Max/MSP와 녹음된 드럼 오디오 샘플을 사용했습니다. Max/MSP Object 정보 수집에 AI를 사용했습니다.

title: Audio-to-MIDI Editor
description: A transcription and MIDI editing prototype with reference-MIDI scoring and recorded seven-song leave-one-song-out drum evaluations.
question: Can AI ease live preparation while preserving the artist’s musical expression?
body: Preparing a recording for a live performance often involves transcribing parts and editing them in a DAW. I am building Trackform to make the first draft easier to create and revise.

The prototype supports piano, general audio, bass, and drum transcription, plus Demucs stem separation. Piano mode uses Transkun and an audio-based sustain correction step. Users can move, resize, audition, and export notes in a browser piano roll.

The Next.js interface and FastAPI processing pipeline can also be packaged with Tauri. Alongside the editor, I built an evaluation pipeline with six bass and eight drum WAV/MIDI reference pairs. Bass scoring uses mir_eval precision, recall, and F1 with 50 ms onset and 50 cent pitch tolerances, without requiring offset matches; separate diagnostics cover octave shifts, timing, and duration. Drum scoring matches instrument classes and onsets with a 50 ms tolerance.

To locate the bottleneck between separation and transcription, I compare three inputs to the same transcriber: the mixture, the Demucs-separated stem, and the reference stem. Saved baselines cover seven synthetic drum mixtures and a second set with the accompaniment separated again to reduce residual drums. The baseline records artifact hashes, the model and device, and deterministic processing assumptions for regression checks.

I also implemented synthetic-mix generation, leave-one-song-out (LOSO) evaluation configurations and models, and training scripts for octave-error, fragmented-note, and joint note models. These separate error analysis from feature implementation and support comparisons on songs excluded from training.

A saved seven-fold leave-one-song-out run evaluates each synthetic drum mixture with a classifier trained on the other six songs. Mean class-aware onset micro F1 is 0.384 for the mixture, 0.752 after Demucs separation, and 0.763 for the reference stem. The separated-stem F1 ranges from 0.578 to 0.921 across songs, showing substantial variation. These are held-out song results within a small synthetic dataset; real production recordings, MIDI correction effort, and rehearsal preparation time still need evaluation. BPM, key, song structure, lyric cues, and rehearsal playback remain areas for further development and testing.

summary.en: Built transcription, separation, and MIDI editing; seven-song LOSO drum evaluation records mean F1 of 0.384 for mixtures and 0.752 after separation.
summary.ko: 변환·분리·MIDI 편집을 구현했습니다. 드럼 7곡 LOSO 평가에서 믹스의 평균 F1은 0.384, 분리 후는 0.752였습니다.

detail.en: Transcription, separation, editing, and export implemented.
6 bass / 8 drum reference pairs, P/R/F1 scoring, error diagnostics, and LOSO evaluation setup.
detail.ko: 베이스 6곡·드럼 8곡의 정답 쌍, P/R/F1 채점·오류 진단·LOSO 평가 환경 구축.

detail.en: Recorded three-path F1 for 7 synthetic drum mixtures, including 7 folds excluding each evaluation song from classifier training.
detail.ko: 합성 드럼 7곡의 3경로 F1과 평가곡을 분류기 학습에서 제외한 7폴드 LOSO 결과 기록.

detail.en: Editing and rehearsal workflow evaluation planned.

title: CI Interactive Ensemble Room
description: A Korean-language interactive listening prototype for CI users, with sound setup, stem mixing, cue comparisons, and personal reports. Uses pink-noise placeholders; user evaluation is still planned.
question: Can listeners discover their own musical cues—and find them again in a song?
body: What should listeners be able to choose for themselves? Building sound systems for venues and a drum response for one performer led to a Korean-language interactive listening prototype for cochlear implant (CI) users: CI Interactive Ensemble Room. The project has moved from design documents to a clickable browser prototype.

The implemented flow runs from sound activation through six sound-setup steps, an ensemble room, cue questions, reflection, and a personal listening report. Setup covers listening equipment and connection, comfortable volume, left–right balance, tone, instrument levels, and optional bass support. Listeners can revisit these choices from the ensemble room.

In the ensemble room, listeners can solo or mute cajon, double bass, and trumpet, change their levels, loop a section, or alternate between sounds. Optional lanes, waveforms, spectra, and performer animations follow audio timing. A listen-first sequence moves from sound alone to visual guidance and back to listening.

Two cue-question sets use comparisons and reflections without correct answers or scores. The report describes patterns in the current session and lets listeners revise their own explanations. Settings, interaction logs, and responses are stored in the browser; JSON and CSV export and full data deletion are implemented. The prototype uses React, TypeScript, Web Audio, and Canvas 2D.

The audio is still a placeholder: each instrument uses independent pink noise, with no real recordings or pitched melody. The first song structure follows Happy Birthday to You; the second song is undecided. The pitch comparison substitutes a change of noise frequency band, so it cannot yet test musical pitch perception. The interface and audio controls are implemented, but music-listening benefits remain untested.

The repository records browser checks on 23 October 2026 for the main flow, audio-node levels, mobile and desktop layouts, and automated accessibility checks. These are implementation checks, not results from CI participants. Next steps are selecting the second song, recording stems and comparison clips, checking real-device playback and latency including Bluetooth and CI streaming, and conducting initial usability sessions with 2–5 CI users. Longer-term learning and transfer to unfamiliar music require a separate study.

summary.en: Built sound setup, an interactive ensemble room, cue comparisons, and listening reports. Pink-noise prototype; CI user evaluation is still planned.
summary.ko: 소리 맞춤·합주실·단서 질문·청취 리포트를 구현했습니다. 핑크노이즈 시험판이며 CI 사용자 평가는 앞으로 진행합니다.

detail.en: Literature-based system design and website scope documented; the first browser prototype is implemented.
detail.ko: 문헌 기반 시스템 설계와 웹 구성안을 정리하고 첫 브라우저 프로토타입으로 구현했습니다.

detail.en: Sound setup, ensemble controls, cue questions, reports, and local export implemented with pink-noise audio.
detail.ko: 핑크노이즈로 소리 맞춤·합주실 조작·단서 질문·리포트·데이터 내보내기를 구현했습니다.

detail.en: Select the second song and replace placeholder stems and comparison clips with real recordings.
detail.ko: 두 번째 곡을 정하고 자리표시 스템과 비교 클립을 실제 녹음으로 교체할 예정입니다.

detail.en: Check playback, decoding, latency, and screen-reader use on phones, Bluetooth, and CI streaming.
detail.ko: 휴대전화·블루투스·CI 스트리밍의 재생·디코딩·지연과 화면 낭독기 사용을 확인할 예정입니다.

detail.en: Participant interviews and usability sessions with 2–5 CI users remain planned; no user findings yet.
